turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How are you doing today, sir?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Honestly, I'm pretty sick today. I've got a lot going on.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How long have you been feeling this way?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, it's been off and on for about a month now.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Has it been getting worse recently?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, it has over the last couple weeks.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What are your symptoms?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, I'm coughing up this yellow phlegm. It feels like everything is in my chest.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What medications have you been taking for this?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I've been taking Allegra D sometimes, but I'm almost out. I need a refill.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What other problems are you having?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My foot keeps breaking out.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Has this improved at all?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, it was for a while, but now it's really bad again.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Have you been diagnosed with any conditions before?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I had, um, tinea pedis before.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How was this treated?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: They gave me Nizoral cream.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It has been getting warmer recently, I don't think that this isn't necessarily a coincidence that you're having these symptoms now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, I work in the flint and it's really hot and humid down there.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What else are you dealing with, sir?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have this wart on my right middle finger, are you able to freeze it off?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Have you ever done that before?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, you have done it before, and it went away.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: If we've done it before, we can do it again.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Cool, can we do blood work, too? I want to check on my prostate.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Well, that's called P S A.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Can I have that done? I'm concerned. I am fifty after all.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Sure, we can check your cholesterol too. I know you have history of it being high.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: You know, I've been working on that. I quit smoking for a while, but I got back into it.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That's good, it's really hard to quit.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, I tried chewing tobacco, but it's not the same.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Be sure to keep trying to quit smoking.

reference_section: This patient presents to the office today for a checkup.  He has several things to go over and discuss.  First he is sick.  He has been sick for a month intermittently, but over the last couple of weeks it is worse.  He is having a lot of yellow phlegm when he coughs.  It feels likes it is in his chest.  He has been taking Allegra-D intermittently, but he is almost out and he needs a refill.  The second problem, his foot continues to breakout.  It seems like it was getting a lot better and now it is bad again.  He was diagnosed with tinea pedis previously, but he is about out of the Nizoral cream.  I see that he is starting to breakout again now that the weather is warmer and I think that is probably not a coincidence.  He works in the flint and it is really hot where he works and it has been quite humid lately.  The third problem is that he has a wart or a spot that he thinks is a wart on the right middle finger.  He is interested in getting that frozen today.  Apparently, he tells me I froze a previous wart on him in the past and it went away.  Next, he is interested in getting some blood test done.  He specifically mentions the blood test for his prostate, which I informed him is called the PSA.  He is 50 years old now.  He will also be getting his cholesterol checked again because he has a history of high cholesterol.  He made a big difference in his cholesterol by quitting smoking, but unfortunately after taking his social history today he tells me that he is back to smoking.  He says it is difficult to quit.  He tells me he did quit chewing tobacco.  I told him to keep trying to quit smoking.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

reference_section: The patient is a 26-year-old female, referred to Physical Therapy for low back pain.  The patient has a history of traumatic injury to low back.  The patient stated initial injury occurred eight years ago, when she fell at a ABC Store.  The patient stated she received physical therapy, one to two visits and received modality treatment only, specifically electrical stimulation and heat pack per patient recollection.  The patient stated that she has had continuous low-back pain at varying degrees for the past eight years since that fall.  The patient gave birth in August 2008 and since the childbirth, has experienced low back pain.  The patient also states that she fell four to five days ago, while mopping her floor.  The patient stated that she landed on her tailbone and symptoms have increased since that fall.  The patient stated that her initial physician examination with Dr. X was on 01/10/09, and has a followup appointment on 02/10/09.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Do those provide any relief?

turns.speaker: patient

reference_section: The patient is a 57-year-old female being seen today for evaluation of pain and symptoms related to a recurrent bunion deformity in bilateral feet, right greater than left.  The patient states she is having increasing symptoms of pain and discomfort associated with recurrence of bunion deformity on the right foot and pain localized to the second toe and MTP joint of the right foot as well.  The patient had prior surgery performed approximately 13 years ago.  She states that since the time of the original surgery the deformity has slowly recurred, and she has noticed progressive deformity in the lesser toes at the second and third toes of the left foot and involving the second toe of the right foot.  The patient is employed on her feet as a hospital employee and states that she does wear a functional orthotic which does provide some relief of forefoot pain although not complete.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How old are you, sir?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I am sixty two year old African American.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Do you have any relevant past medical history?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I do have diabetes, high blood pressure and I had a stroke in the year two thousand and two. I do have weakness on my right side after that. I also had two heart attacks. Ah.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any history of surgery?

turns.text: It shows here that you came to us in two thousand and one for weakness and numbness in your legs. How is that now?

turns.text: What are your symptoms now?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Is that your main concern?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, it is. That is my main problem. I do have pain, but it is not that much of a concern.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: For the last six months, I cannot feel anything hot in my hands. Things slip out of my hand. I don't have any weakness as such, but it's just like that feeling of clumsiness and it's just lots of sensation.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sometimes I feel, like, these jerks in my body, mainly my shoulders and both hands.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Has it been for some time?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It has been like forever but now I am noticing it more than before.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Do you get any kind of tremors?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any neck pain?

turns.speaker: patient

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Have you used anything for your pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, they tried different medicines but only oxycodone helped a little. It does give me sometimes around three hours of relief. Gabapentin did not work at all.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How is your sleep?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I cannot sleep properly because of the pain. It has been for many years. I haven't had a proper sleep.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: When did you get your pacemaker?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It was around six months ago after the heart attack and pacemaker I was transferred to a nursing home. There they stopped my insulin and since then, I'm taking tablets for that.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Do you have any back pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any change in bathroom routine?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Did you ever have any accidents or any injury before all this started?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

reference_section: The patient is a 62-year-old African-American male with a significant past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, previous stroke in 2002 with minimal residual right-sided weakness as well as two MIs, status post pacemaker insertion who first presented with numbness in his lower extremities in 2001.  He states that since that time these symptoms have been progressive and now involving his legs above his knees as well as his hands.  More recently, he describes a burning sensation along with numbness.  This has become a particular problem and of all the problems he has he feels that pain is his primary concern.  Over the last six months, he has noticed that he cannot feel hot objects in his hands and that objects slip out of his hands.  He denies any weakness per se, just clumsiness and decreased sensation.  He has also been complaining of brief muscle jerks, which occur in both hands and his shoulders.  This has been a fairly longstanding problem, and again has become more prevalent recently.  He does not have any tremor.  He denies any neck pain.  He walks with the aid of a walker because of unsteadiness with gait. Recently, he has tried gabapentin, but this was not effective for pain control.  Oxycodone helps somewhat and gives him at least three hours pain relief.  Because of the pain, he has significant problems with fractured sleep.  He states he has not had a good night's sleep in many years.  About six months ago, after an MI and pacemaker insertion, he was transferred to a nursing facility.  At that facility, his insulin was stopped.  Since then he has only been on oral medication for his diabetes.  He denies any back pain, neck pain, change in bowel or bladder function, or specific injury pre-dating these symptoms.

turns.text: Good morning. So, you are here for your follow up today.

turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.text: Update me what happened, why were you in the hospital?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I had a lot of back pain and less of urine output. I always had burning sensation whenever I used to go to the bathroom. So, I went to the doctor, and they said it is kidney stones. I knew something was wrong, but then I started having fever. So, I went to the hospital and they said that it was infection. It all began with my kidney stones.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I see. So how are you feeling now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm feeling better. The burning sensation is gone. Pain has subsided.

turns.text: It says that they put a stent in your ureter. Are you feeling any discomfort with it? Who was your doctor there?

turns.text: No discomfort, I'm just here for my follow up. Doctor X Y Z did operate on me to remove all those stones, the kidney stones. She is a good doctor. She did take care of me. I feel all new now.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That's nice to hear. I'm glad you are feeling okay. You remember I wrote down all the medications with their doses on your progress note, a sheet that we gave to you. Your nephew called me and he said that the prescription was lost and instructions were lost. What happened there?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I don't know. I remember you gave me a paper saying it has all the medicines. It's everything related to them and all the things that I have to do. But I don't know what happened between the hospital and the home. I completely lost it. And I don't know where did it go.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It had instructions to follow up here and also to follow up with Doctor F. Do you have an appointment with Doctor F? You never did call me after the day you were dismissed from the hospital saying that you might have lost the paper that we gave to you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, unfortunately I don't have any appointment with Doctor F. I was not even aware about that, that I have to take an appointment because maybe it was only there in the paper. It completely got out of my mind. Somehow, I did find the prescription paper where all the medicines were and I was able to get them filled and I was taking all my antibiotics and everything else which was there.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I think it was Levaquin. Do you have any more to take?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I do have one more to take.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: So, when are you seeing Doctor X Y Z?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Do I have to see her? I haven't set up anything.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: You do. Any other issues?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, I'm not still feeling very well. I still feel that I'm sick or something like that. It's just that I didn't get my whole self back. You said I got a stent. I have no idea. I don't feel like having one.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Are you the husband?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: Yes, I am. I just wanted to be here with her today.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That's good. Okay, let me explain it to both of you once again. See, she got a ureteral stent. It means that the doctors there, they have made a pathway for the urine to flow around the kidney stone without blocking anything. So, it is to help her overall. She needs to take her medicines and make her appointment with Doctor F. Also, she does need to see if Doctor X Y Z needs a follow up. You can call them and ask. Other than that, everything seems fine.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yep. I will make those appointments. Thank you for your guidance.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Take care.

reference_section: The patient returns today for a followup.  She was recently in the hospital and was found to be septic from nephrolithiasis.  This was all treated.  She did require a stent in the left ureter.  Dr. XYZ took care of this.  She had a stone, which was treated with lithotripsy.  She is now back here for followup.  I had written out all of her medications with their dose and schedule on a progress sheet.  I had given her instructions regarding follow up here and follow with Dr. F.  Unfortunately, that piece of paper was lost.  Somehow between the hospital and home she lost it and has not been able to find it.  She has no followup appointment with Dr. F.  The day after she was dismissed, her nephew called me stating that the prescriptions were lost, instructions were lost, etc.  Later she apparently found the prescriptions and they were filled.  She tells me she is taking the antibiotic, which I believe was Levaquin and she has one more to take.  She had no clue as to seeing Dr. XYZ again.  She says she is still not feeling very well and feels somewhat sick like.  She has no clue as to still having a ureteral stent.  I explained this to she and her husband again today.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Can you tell me your age?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm forty one.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Can you tell me what exactly happened?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: He was cooking, and the hot oil splashed onto his arm.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Did this happen in the coffee shop kitchen?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes. I don't know how the oil splashed but burned my hand. I tried to let it cool down, but the pain was unbearable. I asked my friend to take me to the emergency department here.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: So, this will be the workers' compensation for injury.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I guess, yeah.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: OK, let me see your hand.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: The burn is from the elbow to the wrist. It is mainly on the medial aspect.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: OK, don't worry. We will take care of you.

reference_section: This is a Workers' Compensation injury.  This patient, a 41 year-old male, was at a coffee shop, where he works as a cook, and hot oil splashed onto his arm, burning from the elbow to the wrist on the medial aspect.  He has had it cooled, and presents with his friend to the Emergency Department for care.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Are you ready for home?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Who will help at home?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Just my family.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That is great.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thanks.

reference_section: To home.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It looks like your white blood cell count is normal according to your most recent labs. But, I do want to keep an eye on it given your history of high white blood cells.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's good to hear. I'm glad that it's back to normal.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: However, I must say that I've been having a lot of pain over the past several days.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Where's the pain located?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's mainly my left shoulder and lower back.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Oh, I see. Have you been taking anything for the pain? I remember you were having problems with your lower back the last time you were here. Did you get a chance to see the orthopedist? I believe the left shoulder pain could be due to impingement syndrome.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I haven't taken anything for it yet and I forgot to make an appointment with the doc you recommended. I've been smoking cigs to help with the pain.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I'd advise that you try to wean off smoking for now and consider looking into nicotine patches. Let me see what I can do for the pain and if we can schedule you to see an orthopedist.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thanks, doc. I've had a lot of trouble weaning off cigs for a while now. I've also been eating pretty bad, too. I got to do better.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It'll take time, but with the right diet and regimen, you'll be on better track towards attaining a healthy weight and lifestyle.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, and before I forget-

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I seem to be peeing a lot more these days.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Are you experiencing any other urinary symptoms?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nothing else.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I'll order a urine sample for today's visit to see if you have an infection.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you, doc. And before you write the order, do you know why my one leg is more swollen than the other?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Let me take a look.

reference_section: 1.  Multiple problems including left leg swelling. 2.  History of leukocytosis. 3.  Joint pain involving the left shoulder, probably impingement syndrome. 4.  Low back pain, chronic with obesity. 5.  Obesity. 6.  Frequency with urination. 7.  Tobacco abuse.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How are you feeling?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I feel good. I feel like I am getting stronger every day.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Great! I would like you to continue your exercises at home but please take it slow. Try to stick to the diet we discussed for the next month. Do you have any questions?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No.

reference_section: Activity is as tolerated.  Diet is as tolerated.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hello, sir. What brought you in today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Do you not see the swelling on my right hand and arm? I'm white. The swelling should be noticeable!

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Oh, wow! How did this happen?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I got stung by this huge Yellow Jacket Wasp yesterday. I usually see Doctor X Y Z, but he wasn't available.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I see. Have you ever been stung by a wasp before?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, yeah. Plenty of times. I'm twenty nine right now. I've been getting stung since I was in my early twenties. I usually just swell up like I am right now.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That's good. You never had any severe reactions before?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I did one time before, which is why I came here early to get it checked out.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I see. Just a lot of swelling, correct? What about any anaphylaxis type reactions?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What type of reaction? I don't know what that means, but you're right about the swelling.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It's a reaction that occurs that makes your body go into shock and lowers your blood pressure.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, I get you. No, I've never experienced that before.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Great. Have you ever felt a shortness of breath or your throat closing up before?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nope. That would be really scary though.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Sounds good. Have you ever felt anxious or a fast heart beat after you've been stung?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I haven't. I've only had swelling in the areas I've been stung.

reference_section: He is a 29-year-old white male who is a patient of Dr. XYZ and he comes in today complaining that he was stung by a Yellow Jacket Wasp yesterday and now has a lot of swelling in his right hand and right arm.  He says that he has been stung by wasps before and had similar reactions.  He just said that he wanted to catch it early before he has too bad of a severe reaction like he has had in the past.  He has had a lot of swelling, but no anaphylaxis-type reactions in the past; no shortness of breath or difficultly with his throat feeling like it is going to close up or anything like that in the past; no racing heart beat or anxiety feeling, just a lot of localized swelling where the sting occurs.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: We can give you a shot.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes please.

turns.speaker: doctor

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How are you now? Any bad side effects?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No I feel much better.

reference_section: The patient did request a pain shot and the patient was given Dilaudid of 4 mg IM without any adverse reaction.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.text: Okay, so let's go over the plan again. I'd like you to apply Acticoat dressing daily and make sure you're spending at least eight hours out of the chair for pressure relief. Any questions?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How are you Miss G?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I am good doctor, thank you for asking.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: So, tell me what is going on?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have this ear pain and headache for some time. It's better than before but I still want to get it checked.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay, when exactly did it start?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Um, almost three weeks ago. I am having difficulty hearing. I also feel this pressure on the left side of my sinus causing tooth pain. I went to my dentist yesterday, but my teeth are fine.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay, do you have headache now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, just ear pain and this jaw pain on the left side.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any fever, cough, sore throat, or any cold like symptoms?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, but I have a sinus problem and I suffer from chronic left sided headache.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How old are you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, I am forty nine.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hm, so are you taking any medications for your pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, currently I am just using Cutivate for my eczema. It has helped me a lot, I do need a refill for it.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay I will send a prescription for it to your pharmacy.

reference_section: A 49-year-old female with history of atopic dermatitis comes to the clinic with complaint of left otalgia and headache.  Symptoms started approximately three weeks ago and she was having difficulty hearing, although that has greatly improved.  She is having some left-sided sinus pressure and actually went to the dentist because her teeth were hurting; however, the teeth were okay.  She continues to have some left-sided jaw pain.  Denies any headache, fever, cough, or sore throat.  She had used Cutivate cream in the past for the atopic dermatitis with good results and is needing a refill of that.  She has also had problems with sinusitis in the past and chronic left-sided headache.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My mother died about three or maybe it is four years ago?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I am so sorry to hear that. How did she pass?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: She had lung cancer. My mom didn't talk much about her own health problems.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What about your father? Does he have any health conditions?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My dad has gout. I think he also had blood clots. That is all that I can remember my dad talking about.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay.

reference_section: Ms. A had difficulty providing information on familial medical history.  She reported that her mother died three to four years ago from lung cancer.  Her father has gout and blood clots.  Siblings have reportedly been treated for asthma and GI tumors.  She was unsure of familial history of other conditions such as hypertension, high cholesterol, stroke, etc.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hi sir, let me start by getting your age.

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: He is fifty three!

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: So, tell me what's going on?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: He is complaining of so many things but-

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: But I have a lot of pain from my hernia. That's the number one complaint, but I am also having pain in my lower legs.

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: He has so many issues going on with him, that is why I got him to emergency.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My wife freaks out easily.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Don't worry, let me take a look. So, any nausea and or vomiting?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes both. And I am not sure, but I think I noticed some blood in my stool.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Oh, but you are not sure?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It is questionable!

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I see. And on the scale of one to ten, ten being severe, how will you rate your lower extremity pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Actually, my leg pain has improved considerably. I did have more significant tingling and numbness in the past but now it has improved a great deal.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hm.

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: He has so many medical issues. Here, I have gotten his reports. You can look at them Doctor.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Oh, that's great, thank you for getting these, let me go through them quickly. So, I see you have a history of multiple-

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: Strokes?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yeah, also called as C V A. Peripheral vascular disease. Oh, and heart failure too.

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And you also have a history of multiple bowel ischemia.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, yeah.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: There is a reason why your wife is worried. So, are you taking any medicines currently?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: He is taking Coumadin for his atrial fibrillation. Also, they mentioned it's not optimal for his condition but-

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Oh, I see its subtherapeutic.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, but I am still taking it.

reference_section: This is a 53-year-old man, who presented to emergency room with multiple complaints including pain from his hernia, some question of blood in his stool, nausea, and vomiting, and also left lower extremity pain.  At the time of my exam, he states that his left lower extremity pain has improved considerably.  He apparently had more significant paresthesias in the past and now he feels that the paresthesias have improved considerably.  He does have a history of multiple medical problems including atrial fibrillation, he is on Coumadin, which is currently subtherapeutic, multiple CVAs in the past, peripheral vascular disease, and congestive heart failure.  He has multiple chronic history of previous ischemia of his large bowel in the past.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.text: Is it happening with both hands or one is more than the other?

turns.text: Right side is giving me more problems than the left.

turns.text: Anything else that you noticed?

reference_section: Ms. ABC returns today for followup regarding her cervical spinal stenosis.  I have last seen her on 06/19/07.  Her symptoms of right greater than left upper extremity pain, weakness, paresthesias had been worsening after an incident on 06/04/07, when she thought she had exacerbated her conditions while lifting several objects. I referred her to obtain a cervical spine MRI. She returns today stating that she continues to have right upper extremity pain, paresthesias, weakness, which she believes radiates from her neck.  She had some physical therapy, which has been helping with the neck pain.  The right hand weakness continues.  She states she has a difficult time opening jars, and doors, and often drops items from her right greater than left upper extremity.  She states she have several occasions when she is sleeping at night, she has had sharp shooting radicular pain and weakness down her left upper extremity and she feels that these symptoms somewhat scare her. She has been undergoing nonoperative management by Dr. X and feels this has been helping her neck pain, but not the upper extremity symptoms. She denies any bowel and bladder dysfunction. reference_section: This is a 58-year-old white female suffering increasing right knee pain for number of years prior to surgical intervention.  She was completely refractory to conservative outpatient therapy.  She had undergone two knee arthroscopies in the years preceding this.  They were performed by myself.  She ultimately failed this treatment and developed a collapsing-type valgus degenerative osteoarthritis with complete collapse and ware of the lateral compartment and degenerative changes noted to the femoral sulcus that were proved live.  Medial compartment had minor changes present.  There was no contracture of the lateral collateral ligament, but instead mild laxity on both sides.  There was no significant flexion contracture preoperatively.

turns.text: No, I do not.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Are you sure?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes.

reference_section: Denies the use of alcohol or tobacco.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I will do some examinations on you. I will check your chest and then I will talk to you as I move forward, okay?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm okay with that.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: So, let's see what we have here. Hm, Yeah, just looks good. I do not find anything abnormal.

reference_section: CHEST: The chest examination is unremarkable.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And you mentioned that you have a history of migraine?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, that's correct.

reference_section: History of migraine.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What medications are you taking currently?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, I'm taking Remeron for depression and Ziac for high blood pressure.

reference_section: His only medications are Ziac and Remeron.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: guest_clinician
turns.text: Did you get a chance to review patient's chart?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes, I reviewed his past medical history and family and social history.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: There are no changes, right Mister Jay?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, nothing changed.

turns.speaker: guest_clinician
turns.text: Okay, sounds good.

reference_section: Reviewed.  There are no changes, otherwise.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How are you feeling?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I am well.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: So, we have placed a permanent pacemaker and removed your temporary internal pacemaker.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes.

reference_section: Permanent pacemaker placement after temporary internal pacemaker.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How has our little man being doing?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: Before today he has been doing well, but yesterday he threw up at night and has been very nauseous. He did not complain of stomach issues prior. He is not eating either.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How is his appetite?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: Low. He has no fever, chills, or weakness.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What about coughing, sore throat?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any chest pain or trouble breathing?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any changes in his urination, maybe in color?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any changes in skin color?

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: No. No rash or anything either.

reference_section: The patient prior to today has been very well without any signs or symptoms of viral illness, but yesterday he began to experience symptoms of nausea, had an episode of vomiting last night. Has low appetite. There were no fevers, chills, or malaise. No headache. No congestion or cold. No coughing. He had no sore throat. There was no chest pain or troubled breathing. He did have abdominal symptoms as described above but no abdominal pain. There were no urinary symptoms. No darkening of the skin or eyes. He had no yellowing or darkening of the urine. He had no rash to the skin. There was no local infection at the side of the fingerstick. All other systems were negative.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Well, I have your E K G report, shows you have sinus tachycardia. In other words, your heart is beating faster than normal due to rapid firing of sinus node.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Well, there are no S T changes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hm.

reference_section: EKG shows sinus tachycardia, no acute ST changes.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Good news! No need for any shots today. He is up to date on his immunizations.

turns.speaker: guest_family
turns.text: Good! He hates shots.

reference_section: Up-to-date.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I'm glad to hear that your Afib is under control. I'd like for you to start taking baby aspirin again.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Should I continue taking Nexium?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes, I'd like you to also take Nexium forty M G once a day in order to reduce the risk of an upper G I bleed.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sounds good.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And I ask that you call me immediately if you notice coffee like grounds in your vomit or bloody stool.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: If you have either of these symptoms, then we'll need to put a stop to aspirin.

reference_section: Chronic atrial fibrillation, the patient has been restarted back on aspirin 81 mg at the time of discharge.  Aspirin should be continued with Nexium 40 mg once daily in order to prevent any future occurrence of upper GI bleed.  If the patient has any occurrence of upper GI bleed such as coffee-ground emesis or melena then aspirin should be discontinued.
citation: Ben Abacha et al. 2023, EACL, aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.168
